newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Germans get heroes' welcome after Albania mission.
newsitem.headline: Germans get heroes' welcome after Albania mission.

text.p: German pilots and troops who rescued 120 foreigners from Albania received a heroes' welcome when they returned to their Sarajevo base on Saturday.
Hundreds of German soldiers serving in the NATO-led Stabilisation Force (SFOR) in Bosnia cheered when the six evacuation helicopters landed at their Rajlovac base.
The Germans came under fire from a group of Albanians during the operation on Friday and fired in anger for the first time since World War Two.
The returning helicopters circled over the Rajlovac base in western Sarajevo to cheers from soldiers who climbed on top of buildings and containers to get a better look.
"This is a great success story for German army. The whole camp is out," said Captain Alexander Reinhards.
Evacuation commander Colonel Henning Glawatz, swamped by well-wishers, said: "It was exciting, of course. I am just happy that all of my 91 soldiers are back and no evacuees were wounded."
The pilot commanding the helicopter, which took a hit from the ground, said he did not even notice it until they landed. "It did not go through the armour," Lieutenant Colonel Ingolf Masemann said.
